data.content_ref: inline:The target imposes a necessary condition requiring the checklist to actually conflict with the expert's intuition on at least one case (a non-empty divergence stratum), but this condition is not actually necessary to distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere compliance within a single evaluation. The causal mechanism of checklist contribution can be isolated by comparing a checklist-guided panel against a no-checklist panel (or a structurally-different checklist) on the SAME cases: if the checklist-guided panel outperforms the control on cases where the checklist's rule is objectively validated, the checklist causally contributes even when that rule happens to coincide with what the expert would say. Requiring rule-expert conflict conflates checklist-vs-expert divergence with checklist-vs-no-checklist divergence; the latter is the operative comparison for identifying causal contribution and is available in a single evaluation via counterfactual control conditions the target never acknowledges. The target's own overturn_conditions briefly mention structured-vs-unstructured panel comparisons but then still make the conflict stratum necessary in the main claim, so the argument is self-undermining.
